evidence: THE MAPPING IS PUBLISHED AND FOUR INDEPENDENT CHECKS AGREE WITH IT. The Czech 15-item DSES is Underwood's 16 minus item 5 (Malinakova et al. 2018), so position n maps to Underwood 1-4, 6-16. (1) SPIRIT_15 is the only item with four response levels where the other fourteen have six, which is where the renumbering puts Underwood's closeness question, and two papers from this group describe the Czech form the same way -- 14 six-point items plus a four-point closeness item. (2) The suffixes on SPIRIT_12_ALTR and SPIRIT_13_PRIJ name altruism and acceptance, and the renumbering puts 'selfless caring' and 'accept others' at exactly 12 and 13. (3) THE STRONGEST CHECK TESTS ALL FIFTEEN POSITIONS AT ONCE: under this mapping exactly six of the fourteen frequency items do not mention God, and those six are precisely the six weakest correlates of the closeness item (+0.195 to +0.615, against +0.670 to +0.789 for the eight that do), with a clean gap between the groups. A renumbering shifted by even one item moves a God item into the low group or a non-God item out of it. (4) Cronbach's alpha from the live data is 0.958 against the paper's reported 0.96. DIRECTION WAS A REAL CONFLICT AND THE DATA RESOLVED IT: the source paper's own anchors and its 'higher score = more spiritual' clause contradict each other, and two other papers from the group state the anchors reversed; the SCBCS compassion mean, whose direction is stated unambiguously, correlates -0.317 with the DSES mean while the same paper reports a positive compassion-spirituality association, which fixes 1 = 'Many times a day'. SPIRIT_15 correlates +0.680 with the other fourteen, so it runs the same way. Item set matches at 15 and resp sets match exactly. WHY PARTIAL: route 3 separates two classes of six and eight, not fifteen individuals, so the ordering within each class rests on the published renumbering rather than on this data.

THE PUBLISHED DESIGN CARRIES A HARD ARITHMETIC CONSTRAINT AND IT HOLDS EXACTLY. The paper says the seven discrete-emotion ratings 'had to sum up to 100%'; in the live data they sum to exactly 100 on all 2,184 rating occasions, while the four VAS ratings are unconstrained and range from 0 to 301. That assigns every item to its block without reference to the item names -- moving any one emotion item into the VAS block breaks the sum -- which is the strong form of the check, because the names are the only thing a careless extraction would have relied on. The eleven codes are the eleven rating columns of the deposit's 'Observer ratings.csv', taken verbatim by data/tears.R. Item set matches at 11 and resp sets match exactly.
